text: Hi Lorraine, quick one before I close out the week. The Bramble Bakery bank feed is still missing the Feb 3 deposits from the Saturday market. Can you check whether they went to the old checking account? I can't tie out March until those are in Closebook.

Priya, I finished the first pass on Sycamore for Tidewater. Got 214 transactions cleaned up but there are still around 40 ghost bills from the old Bill.com import. I'll start the dupescrub tomorrow morning and flag anything weird for you.

Note to self: Bramble card payouts land T+2 but Square fees come out net, so the deposit never matches the sales report. Book the fees to the processing expense account, then reclass the gross. Don't forget the chargeback netting on the 14th.

Thanks Renee, the Oakline binder came through fine. Can you send the June payroll register from Gusto when you get a chance? I want to start the splitback for the hygienist wages before the migration.
Lunch at the usual place? I can do 12:30 but I need to be back by 1 for a call with Hal.

Hal, Tidewater's 2024 books are about 60 percent cleaned up. Remaining work is the accrual true-up on the print run deposits and clearing the suspense account. I expect to have Project Sycamore closed by the end of next week, pending your sign-off on the inventory count.

Note to self: Oakline's Gusto import double-posted the employer taxes for two pay periods. Need a reversing JE and check whether the stub entries from the Bill.com sync also hit. Tell Dewey before he re-runs anything.

Hey Keisha, can you pull the AP aging for Marrow Coffee as of Friday? Just the open items over 60 days, I need them for the Closebook review on Tuesday. Thanks for picking up the bank rec last week, it looked great.
Lorraine, sorry for the back and forth. Found it: the Feb 3 deposits went to the old account ending 4417 and I've moved them over. Your March feed should be clean now, can you confirm on your end?

Priya, can you look at the gapfill JE I posted for Tidewater? The vendor credit from Brightline Paper has no matching bill so I parked it in suspense. I think it's a cutoff issue but I'd rather you confirm before I reclass.
Quick reminder to self: the 1099-NEC vendor list has to be locked before January. Check the W-9 status for the freight vendors, two of them still show as LLCs with no EIN on file.

Thanks so much for the coffee last week, Tomasz. The Bill.com sync is running better now, but the approval routing still sends everything to Renee instead of Hal for Tidewater. Could you check the approver mapping on your side?

Hal, the sales tax filing for Q1 is due on the 20th. I need the taxable sales split by county before I can draft it. If you can send the POS export by Wednesday that gives me enough time to tie it to the bank deposits.

Note to self: Sycamore checklist has 14 items, 9 done. Still open: inventory count tie-out, the payroll liability rollforward, the loan interest split, the card reconciliation for the two Amex cards, and the accrued PTO schedule.
Keisha, the Oakline close is on hold until Renee sends the time sheets. Don't post the payroll accruals yet. Just keep working the AR aging and let me know if anything looks off.
Dewey, can you tell me when the Gusto tax filing cutoff is for the Oakline quarter? I think they filed late last year and I want to make sure the penalty doesn't get pushed onto the June close.
Lunch tomorrow? Priya said she's buying if we finish the Sycamore review before 3.

Lorraine, the bank rec for March is done and the variance is zero. The only open item is one ACH return from the landlord, which I'll reverse once the notice comes through. Let me know if you want the summary emailed or dropped in the shared folder.

Note to self: Bramble's tip pool deposits are landing as undeposited funds in QuickBooks every Friday. Make a standing rule so they go to the wage clearing account, not revenue. Mention it to Keisha so she doesn't reclass them by hand again.
Hi Renee, thanks for sending the time sheets so fast. I'll get the accruals posted today and have the June close draft to you Thursday. Please tell Dewey not to re-run the Gusto sync until I say so.

Priya, Sycamore is at 11 of 14 now. The loan interest split is ugly because the lender sent two statements with different dates. I'm going to take the cash-basis view for the stub period and footnote it so Hal understands the swing.

Hal, quick heads up, the inventory count came in $3,140 lower than the perpetual record. I think it's a shrink entry from the spoiled roast batch in February. Can you confirm whether the write-off was approved? I want to book it right before the close lock.

Note to self: the Oakline migration from Gusto to the new payroll cutover is set for Oct 1. Need a cutover checklist: final YTD pull, liability zero-out, opening balances in Closebook, and the splitback for employer share on the dental assistants.

Tomasz, the Bill.com export keeps dropping the memo field on recurring bills. Do you know if that's a mapping limit or something we can change in the sync settings? It breaks the vendor matching on my side.

Lorraine, you were right about the fuel card. The Marathon charges were coming through twice from the Plaid feed. I've set up a dupe rule and reversed the extras. Your April numbers should drop about $480.
Thanks for lunch yesterday. I know the Sycamore timeline is tight but I think we'll make it, probably by the 24th. Let's grab coffee Friday if your kid's game is cancelled again.

Keisha, when you do the card rec for the Amex, check every charge over $250 against the receipt folder before you code it. Last month two of them were personal and I had to reverse them after the client closed.

Dewey, the Oakline YTD payroll totals are off by $212 on the Medicare line. Probably a rounding issue on the hourly staff. Can you check whether the register uses the same rounding as the 941? I don't want it to snowball into the year-end W-2s.
Note to self: when reconciling Tidewater, the Brightline vendor credit finally matched to bill 8841. Clear the suspense entry, then close the gapfill JE and mention it to Priya on the review call.
Hi all, the Closebook template got an update. There's a new tab for the accrual true-up and the old liability tab got renamed. Please don't copy last month's file forward or the formulas will break.
Renee, quick question. Did the dental hygienists ever get the new PTO policy, or are they still on the old accrual rule? The payroll cutover depends on it, and I want the split right before October.

Priya, thanks for the review notes. I agree on the loan interest, I'll reclass it to the correct period. On the freight vendors, I'm going to ask for W-9s again since the first request got lost in someone's inbox.

Hal, the Tidewater sales tax for Q1 is drafted. Total tax due is $4,912 across the two counties. I'll send the filing packet over once you confirm the POS export matched the bank deposits within the rounding tolerance.
Note to self: text Lorraine about the signed lease before filing the Bramble annual return. Her accountant asked for the lease expense schedule, and I don't have the rent escalation clause yet.
Hey Keisha, the Sycamore binder needs tabs for each close item. Can you set them up the same way as the Oakline binder? Use the blue tabs for the tax items and the gray ones for the bank recs.

Lorraine, the Bramble POS sync failed again on Tuesday. Two days of sales are missing from the feed. I've manually imported them from the CSV, but the totals won't tie until the sync is fixed. Can you ask the vendor to look at it?
Tomasz, thanks for the update on the approver mapping. It's working now and Hal is getting the Tidewater approvals. Renee's still getting copies on the Oakline bills, which is fine for now.

Note to self: the Oakline dental supply vendor sends bills to a generic inbox. Need a vendor alias so the bills match the right entity. Otherwise the splitback gets messed up and Priya has to fix it at close.
Quick lunch call tomorrow? Not a big deal, I just want to talk through the cutover plan before Dewey gets involved. Maybe 11:45 at the cafe?
Hal, I know the inventory write-off was a surprise. I've attached the spoilage log and the photos from the walk-in cooler. Once you approve, I'll post it before the Sycamore lock on Friday.
Priya, Sycamore is finally done except for the inventory tie-out, which is waiting on Hal. The trial balance ties to the bank rec within a dollar. I'll lock the period Friday once he signs off.
Note to self: the Oakline cutover is in six days. Final Gusto pull is due Wednesday. Make sure the liability zero-out JE is in the staging tab before the new payroll goes live, not after.
Lorraine, the Bramble annual return is with your CPA now. They asked for the mileage log, the lease schedule, and the card statements from Q4. I'll upload everything to the shared drive by noon.

Renee, the cutover went smoothly. Payroll ran this morning and all the employer taxes posted to the correct accounts. I'll send the October close package once the bank feed updates, probably Thursday afternoon.

Hey Dewey, thanks for catching the rounding issue on the Medicare line. Can you send me the corrected register so I can update the YTD in Closebook? I want to make sure the W-2 totals line up before year end.
Note to self: the quarterly estimated tax reminder for Hal is due Jan 15. Gather the year-to-date P and L by early January and run the safe harbor math against last year's total liability.
Tomasz, I'm seeing a sync lag on the recurring bills again. Some of the Tidewater vendor bills are landing two days late. Is there a known issue with the nightly job, or is it my side?

Priya, the Brightline vendor credit is cleared and the gapfill is closed. I've documented the reclass in the Sycamore notes tab so the reviewer can see the whole trail. Let me know if you want anything else before the lock.
Hi all, the month-end close for Marrow Coffee moved to the 8th because Dana is traveling. Please send any receipts or invoices to the shared inbox by the 5th so I have time to post them.
Lunch on Thursday? I'll buy if you help me figure out the Amex rec. Seriously, it's been three hours and I'm still off by $37.

Lorraine, the Q4 payroll tax deposits for Bramble were made on time, but the state unemployment payment shows a small underpayment. I'll file the correction this week, and the penalty should be under $25.

Note to self: the Oakline splitback needs to be rebuilt for the new payroll setup. The old mapping table points to the Gusto accounts that no longer exist. Rebuild it before the November close or the reports will look wrong.
Renee, can you confirm the new hire start date for the front desk person? I need it to set up the payroll accrual and make sure the first check doesn't get coded to the wrong location.
Hal, the Q3 sales tax return is filed and the confirmation is in the shared folder. The total paid was $4,912. Let me know if you want the estimated tax schedule emailed separately.
Keisha, nice work on the AR aging. Two of the 90-day balances look like duplicates from the old Bill.com export. Can you run a dupe scrub on the Marrow Coffee list before Dana's review on the 8th?

Note to self: the Closebook template has a broken lookup on the cash flow tab after the update. Fix the range so it covers the new accrual tab, then recheck every month against last year's numbers before anyone uses it.

Priya, I know the Sycamore lock took longer than planned, but the trial balance is clean and the notes are complete. I'll write up the lessons for the next catch-up job so we don't get stuck on suspense again.
Thanks for the reminder about the holiday schedule. I'll be out the 24th and 25th, and I'll be checking email on the 26th only if something urgent comes in from Lorraine or Renee.

Hal, the estimated tax reminder for January is coming up. I'll send a rough number based on the year to date by the 5th so you have time to pay before the 15th. Let me know if the inventory write-off changed anything.

Quick note to self: start a fresh Closebook file for December. Copy the template, not last month's tabs, and keep the accrual tab hidden until the true-up is ready. Ping Priya before the 5th to schedule the review.
